title.en: How to Host a Static Website on Raspberry Pi 5 (2025 Beginner Guide) 🌐🍓
title.es: Cómo Alojar tu Web Estática en una Raspberry Pi 5 (Guía paso a paso 2025) 🌐🍓

content.en:
**Looking to build and host your own website with a Raspberry Pi 5 in 2025?** You're not alone — more devs and makers than ever are going full DIY with self-hosted sites. Here’s a quick, modern guide to setting up a static website server with Raspberry Pi, NGINX and your own rules.

---

## 🧠 Why Self-Host a Website with Raspberry Pi?
- 💰 **Ultra-cheap** solution (under $100 total)
- 🚫 **No monthly hosting fees**
- 🔐 **100% ownership**: your server, your rules
- 📡 **Great for learning** Linux, networks, and NGINX
- 🛠️ Perfect side-project for devs and hobbyists

---

## 🧰 What You’ll Need
- 1x Raspberry Pi 5 (with active cooling)
- 1x MicroSD card (32GB+)
- Internet connection (Ethernet or Wi-Fi)
- Your static website (HTML, CSS, JS folder)
- (Optional) Cloudflare account for tunneling

---

## ⚙️ Step-by-Step Setup: Raspberry Pi as Web Server

1. **Flash Raspberry Pi OS** with the official [Raspberry Pi Imager](https://www.raspberrypi.com/software/)
2. Boot and enable SSH, then update everything:
```bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade
```
3. **Install NGINX**, the lightweight web server:
```bash
sudo apt install nginx
```
4. Copy your website files into the server directory:
```bash
sudo cp -r your-site-folder/* /var/www/html
```
5. Restart NGINX to serve your site:
```bash
sudo systemctl restart nginx
```

🎉 Done! You can now access your website via your Pi’s local IP address.

---

## 🌍 Make It Public Without Port Forwarding
Don’t want to mess with your router? Use:
- 🌐 **Cloudflare Tunnel** (Zero Trust, free)
- 🔄 **Tailscale** (VPN-based local network)

Both let you expose your Pi securely online with **zero port forwarding**. Recommended for beginners.

---

## 🧪 Real-World Example: Hosting braisgf.dev
I host [braisgf.dev](https://braisgf.dev) on a Raspberry Pi 5 with Cloudflare Tunnel and NGINX. It’s fast, reliable, and most importantly — it’s mine. The entire project lives on my desk, and the world can access it 24/7.

---

## 📈 Quick SEO Tips for Your Static Website
- Add a clean `<title>` and `<meta description>` to every page
- Include a `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt` for Google
- Compress and lazy-load images (`loading="lazy"`)
- Use semantic HTML tags (`<article>`, `<section>`, `<main>`, etc.)

---

## 🧠 Final Thoughts
Running a **Raspberry Pi static website server in 2025** is easier (and cooler) than ever. Whether you're learning NGINX or building your online portfolio, it’s the perfect side project for devs who love control.

